id: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-五-书籍-p1

en: 第四章-终点篇-大导寺信辅的前半生-五-书籍
From elementary school onward, Shinsuke loved reading books.
u.src: 信辅从小学开始，就很喜欢阅读图书。

en: The Imperial Library edition of Water Margin at the bottom of his father's book chest was the source that awakened his interest in reading.
u.src: 他父亲书箱底部的那本帝国文库本《水浒传》是引起他阅读兴趣的源头。

en: This frail elementary school boy, whose large head was his only striking feature, read Water Margin over and over by dim lamplight.
u.src: 这个只有一个大脑袋的瘦弱小学生，靠着昏暗的灯光，读了很多遍《水浒传》。

ja: それだけではなかった。
en: Nor was that all; even after he closed the book,
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，即使他合上书本，

en: his mind still constantly pictured the banner of acting for Heaven, the tiger on Jingyang Ridge, and the human legs that Zhang Qing the Vegetable Gardener had hung from the rafters.
u.src: 脑子里仍然始终想象替天行道的旗帜，景阳冈山上的老虎，菜园子张青在屋梁上挂着的人腿。
这些都是想象吗？

en: Yet this imagination was even more real than reality.
u.src: ——可是这种想象比现实还要真实。

en: More than once, wooden sword in hand, he had fought the characters from Water Margin in the yard where dried greens were hanging, soundly defeating Yi Zhangqing Hu Sanniang and the Flowery Monk Lu Zhishen.
u.src: 他曾经数次手里拿着木剑，在挂着晒干菜的院子里和《水浒传》书中里人物——一丈青扈三娘、花和尚鲁智深，打个落花流水。

en: For more than thirty years, this passion had continued to sustain him in his heart.
u.src: 三十多年以来，这种激情一直在他心头支持着他。

en: He remembered spending many days reading books through the night without sleep.
u.src: 他记得自己曾经很多天彻夜不眠的阅读书籍。

ja: それだけではなかった。
en: No, it was not only that.
u.src: 不，不仅仅是这样，

en: Whether he was sitting at his desk, in a vehicle, or in the toilet, and sometimes even while walking, he would lose himself in reading.
u.src: 不管是坐在书桌前、车上，还是上厕所的时候——偶尔甚至连走路的时候也会沉溺在阅读之中。

en: After Water Margin, he never picked up a wooden sword again.
u.src: 从《水浒传》之后，他没再拿起过木剑。

en: Yet many times he had cried and laughed over the plots in those books.
u.src: 然而，他曾经多次因为那本书里的情节哭哭笑笑。

en: In other words, he had already entered a self-forgetting state of complete empathy.
u.src: 换言之，已经进入了“完全移情”的忘我境界。

en: He himself had all but become one of the characters in the books.
u.src: 就连他自己也简直成了书里的人物了。

en: At one time, like the Buddha of India, he had been reincarnated countless times.
u.src: 曾经，他就像天竺佛祖一样转世了无数次。

ja: イワン・カラマーゾフ、ハムレット、
、ドン・フアン、メフィスト、ルナール
en: He became Ivan Karamazov, Hamlet, Prince Andrei, Don Juan, Mephistopheles, Reynard the Fox, and others.
u.src: 他变成了伊凡·卡拉马佐夫、哈姆雷特、安德烈公爵、唐璜、梅菲斯特、列那狐等等。

en: And this was not a momentary spell of empathy and self-forgetfulness.
u.src: ——并且，这不是一时的移情忘我。

en: One afternoon in late autumn, wanting to ask for a little pocket money, he went to visit his elderly uncle.
u.src: 在一个晚秋的中午之后，因为想要讨要一些零花钱，他去拜访上了年纪的叔父。

en: His uncle was from Hagi in Choshu, and he deliberately kept praising the outstanding achievements of the Meiji Restoration in front of him,
u.src: 叔父是长州萩人，他故意在叔父不停的夸奖明治维新的卓越成绩，

en: lavishing praise without end on people from Choshu, from Murata Seifu to Yamagata Aritomo.
u.src: 从村田清风，到山县有朋等长州出身的人，都夸赞个不停。

ja: ジュリアン・ソレルだと
en: Yet he himself felt that this pale, frail high school student, full of false passion, was less the Daidoji Shinsuke of that time than the young Julien Sorel, the hero of The Red and the Black.
u.src: 然而，他自己也觉得这个充满虚伪激情、神色苍白的文弱高中生，与其说是当时的大导寺信辅，毋宁说是《红与黑》里的主人公于——年轻的连·索海尔。

en: This was the kind of man Shinsuke was: he had learned everything from books.
u.src: 这样的信辅，所有的事情都是从书里学来的。

en: At the very least, one could say that there was not a single thing in me that had not been inspired by books.
u.src: 至少可以说，我没有任何一件事不是从书本里得到启发的。

en: In fact, he was the sort of person who ignored passersby on the street in order to think about life.
u.src: 事实上，他是一个为了思考人生而无视街头行人的人。

en: Or rather, instead of observing passersby, he preferred to think about the lives found in books.
u.src: 或者说，与观察行人相比，他更愿意思考书本里的人生。

en: Perhaps one could say that this was his indirect way of understanding life.
u.src: 或者可以说这是他理解人生的曲线手段吧！

en: But to him, the passersby on the street were nothing more than ordinary passersby.
u.src: 可是，对于他来说，街头行人不过是普通行人罢了。

en: To understand their lives, to understand their love, their hatred, and their vanity, he had only one method: reading books.
u.src: 他为了理解他们的人生——理解他们的爱，理解他们的憎恨，理解他们的虚荣心，唯有读书一个方法。

en: Books, especially the novels and plays published in fin de siecle Europe, at last opened scene after scene of human comedy in his austere heart.
u.src: 书籍，尤其是世纪末欧洲出版的小说和戏剧，终于在他冷峻的心里，开启了一幕幕人间喜剧。

en: No, it would be better to say that they showed him his own soul, undivided by good and evil; and beyond his own life, they also let him see the natural beauty of the streets of Honjo.
u.src: 不，毋宁说是让他看到了自己不分善恶的灵魂，不仅限于他自己的人生，他也因此看到了本所街町的自然之美。

en: Yet what made his eyes sharper in looking at nature was still the inspiration of a few beloved books, especially the haikai of the Genroku era.
u.src: 但是，让他观看自然的眼睛更加锐利的依然是靠几本喜欢的书的启发——尤其是元禄时代的绯谐。

en: It was precisely because he had read such haiku as "near the capital, seeing the shape of the mountains," "in the turmeric fields, the autumn sky is clear," and "a heron cries as it flies through the dark night" that he discovered an unprecedented natural beauty in the streets of Honjo.
u.src: 正是因为他读了那些绯句，诸如，“近京城观山形”、“郁金田秋高气爽”、“黑夜飞过苍鹭啼”等，他才发现本所街町前所未有的自然之美。

en: For Shinsuke, this process of moving from books to reality was truth itself.
u.src: 这种从“书籍到现实”的过程，对信辅来说就是真理。

en: In the first half of his life, he too had felt affection for several women.
u.src: 他在自己的半生中也曾对几个女子有过爱慕之情。

en: But this did not teach him the beauty of women outside of books.
u.src: 但这并没让他了解到书本之外的女性之美。

ja: ゴーチエ、バルザック、トルスタンの
en: Only through the ordering of Gautier, Balzac, and Tolstoy did Shinsuke come to know the beauty of a woman's "ears translucent in the sunlight" and "the shadow of eyelashes falling on her cheeks."
u.src: 从戈蒂耶、巴尔扎克、托尔斯坦的梳理，信辅才了解到女性“穿透阳光的耳朵”和“落在脸颊上的睫毛的剪影”的美好。

en: Even now, these are still the kinds of feminine beauty that Shinsuke admires.
u.src: 时至今日，信辅欣赏的女性之美还是这些。

en: If he had not learned these things from books, perhaps he would only have known that women were female.
u.src: 如果不是从书本里学到了这些的话，可能他只能知道女性就是雌性吧。

en: However, Shinsuke was very poor and could not buy the books he wanted to read as freely as he wished.
u.src: 可是，信辅很是贫穷，没办法随心所欲的买自己想要阅读的书。

en: So he devised ways to solve this difficulty: first, libraries; second, rental bookshops; and third, pinching pennies so hard that others made fun of him.
u.src: 因此，他想办法来解决这个难题，第一是图书馆，第二是租书店，第三是让别人讥讽的省吃俭用。

en: He always remembered clearly the rental bookshop facing the large drainage ditch, the kindly old woman in the shop, and even her side work making ornamental hairpin flowers.
u.src: 他始终清楚的记得面对大水沟的租书店，租书店里的慈祥老婆婆，还有老婆婆做簪花的副业。

en: The old woman thought this little young master, who had just started elementary school, was innocent.
u.src: 老婆婆认为这个刚上小学的“小少爷”是单纯的。

en: But before he knew it, this little young master had learned the trick of pretending to look for books while actually reading them on the sly.
u.src: 但是，这个“小少爷”却在不知不觉中学会了假装在找书，实际是在偷看书的办法。

en: He also remembered clearly Jimbocho twenty years earlier, when secondhand bookshops filled the whole street and sunlight often shone on the Kudan slope behind their roofs.
u.src: 他也清楚的记得，二十年前的神保町，旧书店布满整条街，阳光常常照耀在旧书店屋顶后面的九段斜坡。

en: Needless to say, in those days Jimbocho had no streetcars, and not even horse-drawn carriages.
u.src: 不必多说，当时的神保町不仅没有电车，就连马车也没有。

en: As a twelve-year-old elementary schoolboy going to the Ohashi Library, he was always hurrying back and forth along that street with his lunch box and notebook tucked under his arm.
u.src: 他，一个十二岁的小学生为了去大桥图书馆，总是在胳膊下夹着便当和笔记本，频繁的往返奔走在那条街上。

en: From the Ohashi Library to the Imperial Library, the distance between the two was about one and a half ri.
u.src: 从大桥图书馆到帝国图书馆，两者相距约莫一里半的路程。

en: His first impression of the Imperial Library was vivid: he was afraid of the high ceiling, afraid of the tall windows, and afraid of the countless readers filling the countless chairs.
u.src: 他对帝国图书馆的第一印象很深——他害怕挑高的天花板，害怕高大的窗子，害怕坐满无数椅子的无数看书人。

en: Fortunately, however, after he had gone two or three times, that fear gradually disappeared.
u.src: 但是，幸亏在去了两三次后，这种害怕就逐渐消失了。

en: Before long, he came to feel familiar affection for the reading room, the iron ladders, the card catalog cabinets, and the basement dining hall.
u.src: 很快，他就对阅览室、铁梯子、书卡柜子、地下食堂有了亲切感受。

en: Later, he also came to use the libraries of universities and high schools.
u.src: 后来，他也会使用大学和高中的学校图书馆。

en: Among the several hundred books, there were dozens that he loved best, but...
u.src: 在数百本书籍里，他最喜欢的有几十本书，但是——

en: But what he loved most were still the books he had bought himself; no matter what their contents were like, he loved those books.
u.src: 但是，他最喜欢的还是自己所购买的书，无论内容怎么样，他都是喜欢这些书。

en: In order to buy books, Shinsuke never set foot in a cafe.
u.src: 为了买书，信辅从不踏足咖啡厅。

en: But his spending money was never enough.
u.src: 但是，他的零用钱总是不够用。

en: Because of this, every Wednesday he had to go to a relative's house to tutor a middle school student in mathematics.
u.src: 为此，他每周三都不得不去亲戚家教中学生数学。

en: Even so, there were still times when he ran short of money, and then he had no choice but to resort to selling books.
u.src: 即便这样，钱还是有不够用的时候，他就不得不的采用买书的办法了。

en: But the price he got for selling a book was not even half of what he had paid for it.
u.src: 但是，卖书的价格连买书价格的一半都没有。

en: And that was not all: selling books he had treasured for years to a secondhand bookstore was, for him, nothing short of a tragedy.
u.src: 不仅仅是这样，把常年珍藏的图书卖给旧书店，这种事对他来说简直是个悲剧。

en: Once, on a night when light snow was falling, he went to Jimbocho and made the rounds of one secondhand bookstore after another.
u.src: 曾经，他在某个下小雪的夜晚，到神保町一家又一家逛旧书店。

ja: ツァラトゥストラはかく
en: In one of those secondhand bookstores, he saw a copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra.
u.src: 他在其中某家旧书店看到了一本《查拉图斯特拉如是说》。

ja: ツァラトゥストラはかく
en: It was no ordinary copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra; it was the very copy, marked with his own handwriting, that he had sold just over two months before.
u.src: 那不是一本普通的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》，那是两个多月前他才卖掉的那本沾有自己手迹的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》。

en: Standing there in the bookstore, he read that copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra once more, and the more he read, the less he could bear to part with it.
u.src: 他站在书店里，又读了一遍那本《查拉图斯特拉如是说》，越看越舍不得。
“这本书多少钱？”

en: After standing there for more than ten minutes, he took Thus Spoke Zarathustra in his hand and asked the bookstore owner.
u.src: 站了十几分钟，他拿着《查拉图斯特拉如是说》问书店老板娘。

en: One yen and sixty sen, but I will make it a little cheaper for you!
u.src: “一圆六十钱，给你便宜一点吧！

en: One yen and fifty sen will do.
u.src: 一圆五十钱就可以了。”

en: Shinsuke remembered clearly that at the time he had sold this book for only seventy sen.
u.src: 信辅清楚的记得，当时他这本书只卖了七十钱。

en: After haggling for ages, he finally managed to buy the book back for one yen and forty sen, twice the price he had sold it for then.
u.src: 讨价还价半天，好不容易才以一圆四十钱，也就是当时卖价的两倍，最后把书又买了回来。

en: On that snowy night, both the houses on either side of the street and the streetcars passing along the road had a subtle sense of stillness about them.
u.src: 下雪的夜晚，不管时候街道两边的住户，还是路上开过的电车，都有种微妙的寂静感。

ja: ツァラトゥストラはかく
en: As he walked through the streets and made his way back along the distant road to Honjo, he kept thinking now and then of the iron-gray copy of Thus Spoke Zarathustra tucked inside his coat.
u.src: 他走过街道，回到很远的本所路上，不时记挂着怀里的那本铁灰色封面的《查拉图斯特拉如是说》。

en: At the same time, he could not help mocking himself under his breath again...
u.src: 与此同时，他嘴里又不由的嘲笑自己……
